title: Conversation schema resolver: normalize OpenAI chat requests/responses for streaming + tool-calls
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Implement a Conversation Schema Resolver service that maps between OpenAI Chat Completions request/response shapes and Redwood's internal streaming, tool/function-calling, and structured-output model. This ticket covers request normalization, response de-framing for streaming chunks, function/tool-call signal translation, and a backward-compatible fallback when clients use legacy Chat Completions semantics. Goal is to make Redwood appear as a first-class OpenAI-compatible endpoint while retaining Redwood runtime features (continuous batching, KV cache, policy routing).
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI-style chat requests (messages + function_call hints) are normalized to Redwood canonical request model without dropping any semantic fields.

Streaming responses are emitted using the OpenAI SSE framing expected by Chat Completions clients (delta tokens, finish_reason events) and include structured-output events when the model emits JSON-schema-constrained payloads.
Function/tool call events from models are translated into Redwood ToolCall objects with deterministic ids and metadata, and are resumable across reconnections.
Legacy clients that expect final aggregated responses receive compatible non-streamed responses when stream=false.
Unit + integration tests validate chunk ordering, message attribution (assistant vs system/user), and idempotent replays for reconnects.
End-to-end performance impact is within the assigned SLO (p50 latency increase < 5ms, p99 < 20ms for adapter layer) for small payloads.
Security review completed for any changes that surface tool metadata or function arguments to downstream systems.
proposal: Add a thin adapter layer in the request ingress path to: 1) coerce OpenAI message arrays into Redwood's internal message frames, 2) honor function_call hints and attach a tool routing plan, 3) inject compatibility headers for downstream runtime. On response, implement a stream liveness multiplexer that converts model token deltas into 'data: {"delta":...}' SSE events, inserts 'tool_call' events when the model switches into a tool invocation state, and emits a final 'done' message with finish_reason and aggregated content when requested. Provide a compatibility mode toggle per-account so enterprise customers can opt into strict OpenAI parity.
technical_notes: Normalization rules: map OpenAI roles (system/user/assistant) to Redwood frames; preserve 'name' fields and function_call.body when present.
Streaming shape: follow OpenAI-style SSE lines with fields {delta, index, finish_reason, tool_call_metadata} encoded as JSON in data lines.

Tool-calls: when model signals a function/tool call, create a ToolCall record with id format 'tc_<short-hash>' and attach routing hints (preferred_runtime, timeout_ms). ToolCall state should be checkpointed into Redis to allow reconnect semantics.

Structured outputs: if client provides a JSON schema hint, validate model output incrementally and emit 'structured_validation' deltas referencing byte ranges to help clients patch partial JSON safely.
Fallback: implement path that composes a full response server-side for stream=false to keep behavior identical to OpenAI for existing clients.
Observability: instrument events for adapter latency, dropped chunks, and tool_call round-trips; add tracing tags for original openai_request_id.
Compatibility tests: create a harness that replays public OpenAI Chat Completions examples, asserting both streamed and non-streamed outputs match canonical shapes.
